sentences.text: THE HON'BLE SMT JUSTICE LALITHA KANNEGANTI CRIMINAL PETITION No.307 OF 2021 ORDER:-

This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 (for short 'Cr.P.C.') to quash the proceedings in F.I.R.No.5 of 2021 dated 04.01.2021 of Vinukonda Town Police Station, Guntur registered for the offences punishable under Sections 188, 420, 270, 272 and 273 read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short "I.P.C.").
2.
The petitioners before this Court are Al to A3 in the above said crime.

3. The brief facts of the case are that while the Police were on duty on 04.01.2021 at about 5:00 P.M.
they found one person i.e. petitioner No.1 at the house of petitioner No.3, who tried to run away on seeing the Police.

But he was apprehended by the Police and on questioning petitioner No.1 confessed that he purchased the said gutka and khaini packets from petitioner No.2 and that the said stock was kept in the house of petitioner No.3.

Basing on the same the present crime is registered against the petitioners and the tobacco products were seized.
4.
Heard Sri Raja Reddy Koneti, learned counsel for the petitioners and learned Public Prosecutor for the State.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that Sections 272 and 273 I.P.C. relate to food safety standards.

Section 272 I.P.C. speaks about adulteration of food or drink intended for sale =x thoy . .
and Section 273 of I.P.C. speaks about sale of Noxious Food or Drink.

He further submits that possession, sale, purchase and transport of banned gutka and tobacco products will not attract the offences as alleged as they do not fall under the definition of food and also do not, spread any disease.
Moreover, the Police have no power to register the offences under above Sections except the designated officers like Food Safety Officer.
Further Section 188 I.P.C. would apply when there is disobedience of an order duly promulgated by a public servant.

As such even Section 188 I.P.C.
is not applicable to the present case.
6. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits the Section 420 of I1.P.C. is also added.
The said section speaks about cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property.
There is neither inducement nor delivery of any property to bring in the ingredients of Section 420 I.P.C.

Therefore,
the same is not applicable to the present case.

7. Learned Counsel for the petitioners placed reliance on the common order dated 18.12.2019 passed by a coordinate Bench of this Court in Criminal Petition Nos.5421 of 2019 and batch, wherein FIRs which were registered under similar circumstances were quashed holding that tobacco does not fall within the definition of "food" as specified under Section 3(i)(j) of the FSS Act and therefore,
registration of FIR under the above sections is not permissible.
Hence, he submits that in terms of the aforesaid orders, this Criminal Petition may be allowed.

As a sequel, pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
